content.comment_body: Can the [product_name] transistor output be used like a typical switch, or does it require a separate supply and return connection? I would like to wire it as shown in my attached sketch, but I'm unable to match the setup described in the [product_name] manual diagram due to physical limitations of my current system. I couldn't find a clear explanation online. Thanks.
If your electrical load operates at 24V DC and requires very little power, you can connect the load directly. Otherwise, it's better to use a relay.

You can connect the load as depicted in your drawing. While [company_name] recommends a different wiring method, following their suggestion isn't strictly necessary. Many users wire the 'M' as you did, since they prefer not to run separate 'M' wires to the [product_name] for every load connection.

analysis.insight_summary: Users want clarity about whether the transistor output of [product_name] can be wired as a standard switch, indicating that available documentation may lack practical guidance for real-world wiring scenarios. Flexibility is needed due to system constraints, and while alternative wiring methods are common, official instructions usually advise a different setup. Uncertainty arises from insufficient context-driven explanations in official documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward guidance about whether the transistor outputs on [product_name] can be wired as switches, and whether using alternative wiring methods—rather than strictly following the manual diagram—is safe and acceptable.
